theme_zh: 跨部門合作：客氣地向別的團隊要資料
summary_zh: 學會用 Could you tell me… / Do you know if… 這類間接問句，客氣又清楚地向其他團隊打聽進度、要資料。

vocab.definition: the moment when one person or team passes a piece of work to another
vocab.example: The handoff between design and engineering went smoothly this time.
vocab.example_zh: 這次設計和工程之間的交接很順利。

vocab.definition: a person or group who is affected by a project and cares about its result
vocab.example: We need to update every stakeholder before we change the launch date.
vocab.example_zh: 改上線日期之前，我們要先通知每一位相關人員。

vocab.definition: how long it takes to finish a request after you receive it
vocab.example: Their usual turnaround time for a data request is three working days.
vocab.example_zh: 他們處理一份資料需求通常要三個工作天。

vocab.zh: 把（某人）拉進來一起討論
vocab.definition: to include someone in a conversation or email so they know what is happening
vocab.example: Let me loop in Priya, since she owns the customer database.
vocab.example_zh: 我把 Priya 拉進來，因為客戶資料庫是她負責的。

vocab.zh: 各自為政、不互通的部門
vocab.definition: a team or department that works on its own and rarely shares information with other teams
vocab.example: When every department works in a silo, simple questions take weeks to answer.
vocab.example_zh: 每個部門都各做各的時候，簡單的問題也要好幾週才有答案。

vocab.definition: a short warning that tells someone about something before it happens
vocab.example: Thanks for the heads-up about the system maintenance on Friday.
vocab.example_zh: 謝謝你先提醒我們週五系統要維修。

vocab.zh: 負責到底的態度；主導權
vocab.definition: the responsibility for a task, so that you make sure it gets done
vocab.example: Mei took ownership of the report and fixed the numbers herself.
vocab.example_zh: Mei 把這份報告扛下來，自己把數字修好了。

vocab.definition: a list of work that is waiting to be done because there hasn't been time for it yet
vocab.example: The data team has a backlog of forty requests, so ours will have to wait.
vocab.example_zh: 資料團隊累積了四十個待處理的需求，所以我們的要排隊。

reading.title: Getting Answers From Another Team
paragraphs: When Kevin joined the marketing team, he thought the hardest part of his job would be the campaigns. He was wrong. The real challenge was getting numbers from the data team. Every request seemed to disappear into their backlog, and waiting for an answer felt like getting a security deposit back from a landlord: possible, but slow.

At first, Kevin sent short, direct messages: "Where is the report? When will it be ready?" The data team was overloaded, and the tone didn't help. Tensions flared up in one meeting, and two of his requests were carried over to the next sprint without explanation.

His manager, Grace, suggested a different approach. Instead of demanding answers, Kevin started asking polite questions: "Could you tell me what your usual turnaround time is?" and "Do you know if there's a better way to submit requests?" He also gave the team a heads-up a week before every big campaign, so they could plan ahead.

The biggest change came when he looped in Priya, the data team's lead, at the start of each project instead of at the end. She explained that the team had just upgraded its tools, and that this was why the handoff had been so slow. Once both sides understood each other, they set up a simple shared calendar.

Kevin still remembers that first month. "We weren't bad teams," he says. "We were silos. Nobody took ownership of the space between us." To make up for his impatient messages early on, he now sends Priya's team a thank-you note after every launch.

questions.q: What made things harder for Kevin at first?
options: The data team was overloaded, and his messages sounded too demanding.
Kevin forgot to submit his requests before the deadline.
Grace told the data team to work on other projects first.
The requests were sent to the wrong department.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段說資料團隊工作量太大（overloaded），而且他直接的口氣也沒有幫助（the tone didn't help）。

questions.q: According to Priya, why had the handoff been so slow?
options: Kevin's team had changed its campaign plans.
Her team had just upgraded its tools.
Her team did not have a shared calendar.
Grace had not approved the requests.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：the team had just upgraded its tools, and that this was why the handoff had been so slow。共用行事曆是之後的解決方法，不是原因。

questions.q: What can we infer about Kevin from the last paragraph?
options: He thinks the data team was mostly to blame.
He is planning to leave the marketing team.
He feels partly responsible for the early problems.
He no longer needs data from Priya's team.
questions.explain_zh: 他說「沒人負責兩隊之間的空間」，還為了彌補（make up for）一開始不耐煩的訊息而在每次上線後寫感謝信，可以推論他覺得自己也有責任。他並沒有怪資料團隊，每次上線後也還在和他們合作。

grammar.point: Indirect questions: Could you tell me where…
grammar.point_zh: 間接問句：Could you tell me where…（把問題放進客氣的句子裡）

guide.key_zh: 問句接在 Could you tell me 後面要改回直述句：主詞在前，拿掉 do/does/did。

uses.label_zh: 有 be 動詞或助動詞（is／are／can／will／has）：移到主詞後面
uses.form: Could you tell me + where + S + is／will V
uses.note_zh: is／are／can／will／has 移到主詞後面，不留在疑問詞後面

uses.label_zh: 有 do/does/did：拿掉它，時態加回動詞
uses.form: Do you know + when + S + V／V-s／V-ed
uses.note_zh: do → 動詞用原形；does → 動詞加 s；did → 動詞改過去式

uses.label_zh: Yes/No 問題：前面加 if 或 whether
uses.form: Do you know + if + S + V
uses.note_zh: if 後面一樣是直述句順序

mistakes.wrong: Do you know what time does breakfast start?
mistakes.right: Do you know what time breakfast starts?
mistakes.why_zh: does 要拿掉，三單的 s 加回 start

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me where is the meeting room?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me where the meeting room is?
mistakes.why_zh: 間接問句不倒裝：is 要放到主詞 the meeting room 後面

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me is the gym open 24 hours?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me if the gym is open 24 hours?
mistakes.why_zh: Yes/No 問題要加 if，而且 is 要放回主詞後面

examples.en: Where is the latest version? → Could you tell me where the latest version is?
examples.zh: 最新版本在哪裡？→ 可以告訴我最新版本在哪裡嗎？

examples.en: When did they send the file? → Do you know when they sent the file?
examples.zh: 他們什麼時候寄出檔案的？→ 你知道他們什麼時候寄出檔案的嗎？

examples.en: Is the dashboard working? → Do you know if the dashboard is working?
examples.zh: 儀表板正常嗎？→ 你知道儀表板是不是正常嗎？

exercises.q: (Where is the latest sales file?) Could you tell me ___?
exercises.answer: where the latest sales file is
exercises.explain_zh: 有 be 動詞：把 is 移到主詞 the latest sales file 後面。

exercises.q: (What time does the dashboard update?) Do you know ___?
exercises.explain_zh: 拿掉 does，三單的 s 加回動詞：the dashboard updates。

exercises.q: (Why did the numbers change last week?) Could you explain ___?
exercises.answer: why the numbers changed last week
exercises.explain_zh: 拿掉 did，過去式加回動詞：the numbers changed。

exercises.q: (Has the data team finished the migration?) Do you know ___?
exercises.answer: if the data team has finished the migration
accept: whether the data team has finished the migration
if the data team has finished it
whether the data team has finished it
exercises.explain_zh: Yes/No 問題前面加 if／whether，has 放回主詞後面：the data team has finished。

exercises.q: (Do the two teams share a calendar?) I was wondering ___.
exercises.answer: if the two teams share a calendar
accept: whether the two teams share a calendar
exercises.explain_zh: Yes/No 問題加 if；拿掉 do，主詞是複數 the two teams，所以動詞用 share，不加 s。

options: how long will the handoff take
how long the handoff will take
how long does the handoff take
how long the handoff does take
exercises.explain_zh: I'd like to know 後面是間接問句，要用直述句順序：主詞 the handoff 在前，will take 在後。其他選項都保留了問句倒裝或多餘的 does。

review.point: Gerund vs infinitive: stop doing / stop to do, remember, try
review.point_zh: 動名詞 vs 不定詞：stop／remember／try 接 V-ing 或 to V 意思不同

exercises.q: The app keeps crashing. Have you tried ___ (restart) it? That sometimes fixes it.
exercises.explain_zh: try + V-ing＝試試看某個方法有沒有用；這裡是建議一個解決辦法。

exercises.q: Please remember ___ (copy) the data team on the email before you send it.
exercises.explain_zh: remember + to V＝記得要去做（還沒做的事）；before you send it 表示是之後要做的。

exercises.q: On my way to the meeting, I stopped ___ (grab) a coffee, so I was a few minutes late.
exercises.explain_zh: stop + to V＝停下來去做另一件事；他停下腳步是為了買咖啡。

guide.key_zh: stop／remember：V-ing＝在做或做過，to V＝接著要做。try：V-ing＝試方法，to V＝努力做到。

uses.label_zh: stop：停掉正在做的事 vs 停下來去做另一件事
uses.note_zh: stop to V 的 to＝為了去做

uses.label_zh: remember：記得做過 vs 記得要去做
uses.note_zh: V-ing＝過去的回憶；to V＝還沒做、別忘了

uses.label_zh: try：試試看某個方法 vs 努力想做到
uses.note_zh: try V-ing＝實驗看看有沒有效；try to V＝想辦法完成（不容易）

mistakes.wrong: Remember locking the door when you leave tonight.
mistakes.right: Remember to lock the door when you leave tonight.
mistakes.why_zh: tonight 還沒發生，是提醒要去做的事 → remember to V

mistakes.wrong: I stopped to check my phone during meetings because it was rude.
mistakes.right: I stopped checking my phone during meetings because it was rude.
mistakes.why_zh: 因為覺得沒禮貌，所以「戒掉、不再做」這個習慣 → stop V-ing；stop to check 是「停下來去看手機」，和 because it was rude 的邏輯不合

listening.title: A quick call with the data team

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Hi Priya, thanks for jumping on. Sorry, I think my connection dropped for a second there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: No worries. You were breaking up a little, but I can hear you fine now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Great. Could you tell me where we are with the campaign data? The launch is next Tuesday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Honestly, it got carried over from last sprint. Our backlog has been huge since the system upgrade.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: I understand. Do you know if the new dashboards are ready yet?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Almost. Mei has been sorting out the access problem all morning, and it's nearly done. Oh, and the old reports were moved last week, so the links you saved don't work anymore.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Good to know. Is there anything I can do to speed things up on the campaign data?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Actually, yes. If you send me the exact fields you need, I can skip the full report.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Perfect. I'll send them today. And do you know what your turnaround time is for something that small?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Probably two days. But please give us a heads-up next time. Things get messy fast when requests come in late.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: That's fair. Next time I'll loop you in at the start, along with the other stakeholders.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: That would really help. Talk soon, and good luck with the launch.

questions.q: Why hasn't the campaign data been delivered yet?
options: Kevin sent the wrong request.
It was carried over because the data team has a large backlog.
Priya was on vacation last sprint.
The launch date was moved forward.
questions.explain_zh: Priya 說 it got carried over from last sprint，而且系統升級後待處理的工作很多（Our backlog has been huge）。

questions.q: What does Priya offer to do?
options: Send only the specific fields instead of the full report.
Move Kevin's launch to next month.
Ask her manager for more staff.
Upgrade the system again.
questions.explain_zh: 她說：If you send me the exact fields you need, I can skip the full report。

questions.q: What can we infer about past requests from Kevin's team?
options: They were usually too detailed.
They were always finished within two days.
They often reached the data team late in the project.
They were sent to the wrong person.
questions.explain_zh: Priya 請他下次早點通知，因為需求太晚進來時事情很容易變得一團亂；Kevin 也說下次會「一開始」就找她，可推論以前常常很晚才提出。

dictation: Do you know if the new dashboards are ready yet?
Mei has been sorting out the access problem all morning, and it's nearly done.
The old reports were moved last week, so the links you saved don't work anymore.

shadowing: Could you tell me where we are with the campaign data?
Do you know if there's anything I can do to speed it up?
Thanks for the heads-up. I'll loop in my manager.
I was wondering what your usual turnaround time is.

prompts.question: You need a file from another team, but you don't know who owns it. Ask politely in one or two sentences.
prompts.question_zh: 你需要另一個團隊的檔案，但不知道是誰負責的。用一兩句話客氣地問。
prompts.sample: Hi, sorry to bother you. Could you tell me who owns the customer report, and do you know if it's been updated this month?

prompts.question: Another team's request has been delayed. Ask them about the timing without sounding pushy.
prompts.question_zh: 另一個團隊的工作延誤了。問他們時間，但不要聽起來在催。
hints: Is there anything I can do to…
prompts.sample: I know you're very busy. I was wondering when you think it might be ready, and whether there's anything I can do to help.

writing.task: Write a short email to another team asking for data you need for a project. Ask at least two polite indirect questions and give them a heads-up about your deadline.
writing.task_zh: 寫一封短信給另一個團隊，請他們提供專案需要的資料。至少用兩個客氣的間接問句，並事先告訴他們你的截止日。
writing.sample:
Hi Priya,

I hope your week is going well. I'm working on the December campaign, and I'll need last quarter's sign-up numbers by the end of next week. I wanted to give you a heads-up now so it doesn't land on you at the last minute.

Could you tell me what your usual turnaround time is for a request like this? I only need three fields, so it may be quicker than a full report. Also, do you know if there's a form I should use instead of email?

Thanks so much for your help. Just let me know if anything is unclear.

Best,
Kevin
checklist_zh: 間接問句用直述句順序（主詞在動詞前面），沒有多出 do/does/did
Yes/No 問題前面有 if 或 whether
清楚寫出需要什麼、什麼時候要

translation.zh: 你知道資料團隊什麼時候會更新儀表板嗎？
translation.en: Do you know when the data team will update the dashboard?
alt: Do you know when the data team is going to update the dashboard?

translation.zh: 可以告訴我這個檔案是不是最新的版本嗎？
translation.en: Could you tell me if this file is the latest version?
alt: Could you tell me whether this file is the latest version?
Could you tell me if this is the latest version of the file?

translation.zh: Mei 已經做完三份報告了，但她從今天早上就一直在處理第四份。
translation.en: Mei has already finished three reports, but she has been working on the fourth one since this morning.
alt: Mei has already finished three reports, but she's been working on the fourth since this morning.

translation.zh: 到目前為止，已經有十二個需求被延到下一個衝刺週期。
translation.en: So far, twelve requests have been carried over to the next sprint.
alt: So far, twelve requests have been moved to the next sprint.

replies.zh: 今天翻譯第 3 題對照「has already finished three（已完成、看結果）」和「has been working on the fourth since this morning（還在做、看過程）」；聽寫第 2 句是 has been sorting out，聽的時候注意弱讀的 has been。

reading.title: The Space Between Teams
paragraphs: Most companies don't have a talent problem; they have a hallway problem. Two departments can each be excellent and still let a project fall apart, simply because nobody owns the work that passes between them. Managers often call this "working in silos," but the phrase makes it sound deliberate. In reality, it's usually a slow drift: each team optimizes for its own goals, its own tools and its own deadlines, until the other side becomes a black box.

The symptoms are easy to spot once you know what to look for. Requests sit in someone's inbox for days because nobody is sure whether they're urgent. People send the same question to three different colleagues, hoping one of them will bite. And when something finally goes wrong, the post-mortem turns into a polite argument about whose job it was in the first place.

The fix is rarely a reorganization. More often, it's a handful of small habits. Teams that collaborate well tend to ask before they assume: "Could you walk me through how your team prioritizes requests?" goes a lot further than "Why is this taking so long?" They flag dependencies early, before anyone is under pressure. And crucially, they name a single person on each side who is accountable for the handoff, so problems don't bounce back and forth like a tennis ball.

None of this requires a new tool or a bigger budget. It requires curiosity about how the other team actually works, and the humility to admit that your own team's priorities are not the only ones that matter. The payoff, though, is real: fewer surprises, faster decisions, and colleagues who pick up the phone when you call instead of letting it ring.

questions.q: What does the writer mean by a "hallway problem"?
options: Offices are too small for teams to meet.
Problems happen in the work that moves between teams.
Employees spend too much time chatting in the hallway.
Companies hire people who are not talented enough.
questions.explain_zh: 下一句解釋：兩個部門都很優秀，但沒人負責「在兩者之間傳遞的工作」（the work that passes between them），所以是指團隊之間的落差。

questions.q: Why does the writer say the phrase "working in silos" is misleading?
options: Silos usually develop gradually rather than on purpose.
Most teams prefer to work alone.
Managers use it to blame junior employees.
It only describes problems with software tools.
questions.explain_zh: 原文說這個詞聽起來像是故意的（makes it sound deliberate），但其實通常是慢慢漂移形成的（a slow drift）。

questions.q: What does the writer most likely think about reorganizing a company to fix collaboration?
options: It is the only solution that really works.
It should happen before any new habits are tried.
It is usually less necessary than changing everyday habits.
It is too expensive for most companies.
questions.explain_zh: 作者說 The fix is rarely a reorganization，通常只要幾個小習慣，最後也說不需要新工具或更多預算，可推論他認為改日常習慣比重組更重要。

listening.title: Who owns the handoff?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Okay, so before we dive in, could you tell me who actually signs off on the data before it reaches us?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Uh, good question. I mean, technically it's Priya, but in practice it kind of depends on who's free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Right, and that's sort of the problem, isn't it? Last month we—

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: I know, I know. Two people each thought the other one had it, and we waited four days. Not our finest moment.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: So what if we just picked one name per project? Doesn't have to be a manager.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: I like that. Though, do you know if your team would do the same on your side?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Absolutely. Kevin's already volunteered, believe it or not.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Ha, after the last launch? He's braver than I thought.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: He's learned a lot. Anyway, shall we try it on the December campaign and see how it goes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Let's do it. I'll run it past Priya this afternoon and get back to you.

questions.q: What caused the four-day delay last month?
options: Priya was on leave.
Each of two people assumed the other was handling the data.
Grace's team sent the request too late.
The data was signed off by the wrong manager.
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 說 Two people each thought the other one had it，兩個人都以為對方在處理，所以等了四天。

questions.q: What does Marcus's comment about Kevin suggest?
options: Kevin has never worked on a launch before.
Kevin is Marcus's manager.
The last launch was difficult for Kevin.
Kevin does not want to take on more work.
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 說 after the last launch? He's braver than I thought，表示上一次上線對 Kevin 來說不順利，所以他主動願意負責讓人意外。

questions.q: What will Marcus most likely do next?
options: Talk to Priya about naming one owner per project.
Start the December campaign on his own.
Ask Kevin to join his team.
Cancel the next meeting with Grace.
questions.explain_zh: 最後他說 I'll run it past Priya this afternoon，會先去問 Priya 這個「每個專案指定一個負責人」的做法。

dictation: Could you tell me who actually signs off on the data before it reaches us?
Two people each thought the other one had it, and we waited four days.

glossary.definition: a slow change that happens without anyone planning it
a meeting after a project or problem to discuss what went wrong
to point out something so that people pay attention to it
responsible for something and expected to explain the result
to give official approval for something
